column1: # Oracle-pinned CLI-flag cases.  ONE source of truth, read by BOTH sides:
#   * tests/cli_e2e.rs   runs `tamarin-rs` on the row's argv and byte-compares
#                        runs the HASKELL oracle on the SAME argv and writes
# Keeping the argv here instead of in each side means a ref can never be
# captured with flags the test does not use.  Add a row, then re-run
# scripts/capture_cli_refs.sh — the test HARD-FAILS (never skips) on a row
#   name       ref basename; <name>.stdout holds the RAW oracle stdout
#   relation   how this row's ref must relate to another row's, compared after
#              both are normalized (build info / processing time / analyzed
#              `=other` = must be IDENTICAL.  This is the anti-vacuity check:
#              a `!=` row proves the flag actually changed the run, and an `=`
#              row states, on the record, that it did not.
#   args       flags, space-separated, before the theory path.  `{FIXTURES}`
# `--derivcheck-timeout=300` is on every row on purpose: the default is 5s, and
# a derivation check that times out under load adds a wellformedness entry to
# stdout, which would make these refs flaky rather than wrong.
# ---- --lemma / --bound (theory: two lemmas, one verified one falsified) -----
# it appends ppWf's second warning line, run.rs's 9-space variant) ------------
# ---- --bound reaching the PARALLEL sibling expansion.  cli_flags_tutorial is
# a byte-copy of the submodule's examples/Tutorial.spthy: its proofs fan out
# (>= 2 cases under Dfs), so `-b=6` cuts inside rayon workers — the pin that
# fails if `PROOF_BOUND` is not re-seeded per worker (search.rs) -------------
# ---- --stop-on-trace (exists-trace search: dfs cuts, none explores; bfs and
# sorry are the two other non-default strategies that reach the solver) -------
# cli_flags_chan_heur is the chan fixture plus an in-file `heuristic: i`
# header; the CLI flag must override it (cli.rs's load-bearing bare-flag
# `=chan_plain` on the record: a rank-nothing oracle degenerates to goal-number
# order, which coincides with the default ranking on this fixture — the spawn
# proof is chan_oracle_pick_last, the flag proof is chan_oracle_only.
